# ChoiceGrid

ChoiceGrid — the same question asked of several rows, as a table. Each cell is the real Checkbox or Radio, named by its row and its column.

Also asked as: matrix question.

**Import:** `import { ChoiceGrid } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ChoiceGrid/ChoiceGrid.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ChoiceGrid/ChoiceGrid.stories.jsx` — Overview, Variants, Layout, Size, InteractionStates, TwoGridsWithoutIds, ReadOnly, Interactive, Keyboard, Unselected, Selected, Hovered, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ChoiceGrid/ChoiceGrid.mdx`

## Usage

Use a choice grid when the same question is asked of several things at once: rate each of these six statements, tick which of these tools each tutor uses. It is a matrix with one question in the column headers and one subject per row.

It is fully controlled. `values` is `{ rowId: columnId }` in `radio` mode and `{ rowId: { columnId: boolean } }` in `checkbox` mode, and the component holds no state of its own.

## Best practices

### `onChange` has two shapes, and only one of them is the new state. {#onchange-has-two-shapes-and-only-one-of-them-is-the-new-state}

```jsx
// radio: the two ids that changed. Merge them yourself.
<ChoiceGrid type="radio" values={v} rows={rows} columns={cols}
            onChange={(rowId, columnId) => setV({ ...v, [rowId]: columnId })} />

// checkbox: the whole new values object, already merged.
<ChoiceGrid type="checkbox" values={v} rows={rows} columns={cols}
            onChange={(next) => setV(next)} />
```

In checkbox mode the merge copies the top level and the row it changes, so the `values` you passed in is left as it was and can be compared against the next one.

### A radio row cannot be unanswered again. {#a-radio-row-cannot-be-unanswered-again}

Selecting a column always sets it; there is no path back to "not answered". If that state is meaningful, add a column for it. "Not applicable" as a real option is better than a row the user cannot clear.

### Keep the grid small. {#keep-the-grid-small}

Every cell is a control, so a six-by-five grid is thirty tab stops. Past that, ask the questions one at a time with Radio group.

### Give the grid a question above it. {#give-the-grid-a-question-above-it}

Do: A question above the grid that every row answers.
Don't: The same grid with no question: nothing says what the scale measures.

### Radio grid for one answer per row. {#radio-grid-for-one-answer-per-row}

The control type tells people how many answers a row takes.

Do: Radios, for one preferred time each day.
Don't: Checkboxes for the same single-answer rows.

### Checkbox grid for several answers. {#checkbox-grid-for-several-answers}

Checkboxes signal that a row accepts more than one answer.

Do: Checkboxes, for every tool each tutor uses.
Don't: Radios, where several tools apply to a row.

### Keep one size per grid. {#keep-one-size-per-grid}

Mixed control sizes make a grid hard to scan. `size` is set per grid, so grids that sit together in one form share it too.

Do: Size 14 across both grids.
Don't: A size 12 grid under a size 14 one.

## Accessibility

- **Every cell is named by its row and its column.** Each input carries `aria-labelledby` pointing at both the row label and the column header, so it is announced as "Punctuality, Agree" rather than as an unnamed radio in a table.
- **Every cell is the real control.** Cells render Checkbox and Radio, so focus, states and read-only behave as they do anywhere else.
- **Radio rows are grouped per row.** Each row's inputs share a `name` built from the grid's id and the row's id, which makes one answer per row and arrow-key movement along it. With no `id` or `name` the grid generates its own base, so two grids on a page never share ids or radio groups.
- **The grid itself has no name.** There is no caption and no `aria-label` on the table. Put the question above it as a heading, and describe the scale in the column headers.
- **The row-header column is empty on purpose.** It carries a visually hidden "Row" so the header row is not a blank cell.
- **On a narrow screen this is a wide table.** Put it in a horizontal scroll area rather than letting the columns crush.

- For one question with several answers, use Radio group.

## Parts

1. **Column headers.** The answer scale. They name every cell in their column.
2. **Row labels.** The subject of each row. They name every cell in their row.
3. **Cells.** A real Radio or Checkbox, centered, with no visible label of its own.
4. **Row-header corner.** Empty on purpose; it carries a visually hidden "Row".

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Each cell shows its Radio or Checkbox at rest, unselected. |
| Hovered | As the Radio or Checkbox in the cell: the input hovered fill and a brand edge. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered look holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | As the control in the cell: a 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Selected | As the control in the cell: the selected bold fill. |
| Read-only | Full contrast, cells stay in the tab order with `aria-readonly`; changes are ignored. |
| Disabled | Cells take the disabled fill and edge and leave the tab order; header text uses a solid muted token, not opacity. |
| Invalid | Not drawn by the grid. Put the message above it and mark the question there. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `--ds-surface-container` on the table, headers, labels and cells. |
| Padding | `--pad-y-md` and `--pad-x-md` on headers, labels and cells. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`. |
| Text | `--ds-text`, body default, or the label font `size` picks. |
| Control | `--checkbox-control-size`, or `--choice-grid-control-size-10` and `-12` through `size`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write column headers as the scale: "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Often". | Bare numbers with no meaning attached. |
| Keep row labels short and parallel; they do not wrap. | A sentence per row. |
| Phrase the question above the grid so every row answers it. | A different question in each row. |
| Keep column headers short and the same length. | A header the person cannot read at a glance. |
